Plant Care Tips

Water Wisely

Most indoor plants prefer to dry out slightly between waterings. When in doubt, wait a day!

Light Matters

Observe your plant's leaves. Yellowing often means too much light, while leggy growth indicates too little.

Temperature Control

Most houseplants thrive between 65-75°F (18-24°C). Avoid placing them near drafts or heating vents.

Fertilize Sparingly

Feed your plants every 4-6 weeks during growing season (spring/summer). Reduce or stop in winter.

Pro Tip: The Finger Test

Insert your finger 1-2 inches into the soil. If it feels dry, it's time to water. If it's still moist, wait a few more days.

All live sessions are recorded and timestamped within 24 hours. You can submit questions in advance, and we answer them on the call. Many alumni participated entirely async and still completed compelling final projects.

Specialty Coffee Brewing Guide

The Golden Ratio

The Specialty Coffee Association (SCA) defines the "Golden Cup Standard" as a ratio of 55g to 60g of coffee per 1 Liter of water. This equates to a ratio of approximately 1:16 to 1:18. Adjust your ratio down (e.g., 1:15) for a stronger, heavier body, or up (e.g., 1:18) for a lighter, cleaner cup.

Over-Extraction

Occurs when you draw too much soluble material out of the coffee. Tastes bitter, dry, hollow, and astringent. Fix by grinding coarser or brewing faster.

Under-Extraction

Occurs when you don't extract enough. Tastes sour, salty, sharp, and lacks sweetness. Fix by grinding finer or extending brew time.

The Importance of Temperature

Water temperature acts as an extraction accelerator. Light roasts benefit from hotter water (93°C–96°C) to extract complex sugars. Dark roasts extract easily and should be brewed cooler (88°C–91°C) to avoid harsh, carbon-like bitter flavors.
